records.statement: User story US-01: As the content operator, I want to create a content project in a web interface by selecting a competition, season and matchday, so that the platform prepares coverage of that matchday.

User story US-02: As the content operator, I want the platform to research the selected matchday (results, teams and scores, dates, standings and competition context) and to show me the progress of the research, so that I receive structured, source-attributed data without collecting it by hand.

User story US-03: As the content operator, I want every fact to be verified independently against reliable sources and marked as verified or not verified, so that content with invented or unverified scores, standings or statistics cannot be approved.

User story US-04: As the content operator, I want the platform to draft the carousel structure, headlines, slide descriptions, social media caption and hashtags from the verified data, so that I start my review from a complete draft.

User story US-05: As the content operator, I want cover, match-result, standings and closing slides generated in the El Deporte Rey GT visual identity from reusable templates, so that every post looks professional and consistent.

User story US-06: As the content operator, I want an automated visual quality check of every slide before my review, so that wrong scores, standings or team names, overflowing text, inconsistent visuals and wrong dimensions are caught.

User story US-07: As the content operator, I want to preview the carousel and captions, regenerate individual slides and explicitly approve the content, so that nothing I have not approved can be exported.
User story US-08: As the content operator, I want to export the approved images and captions, so that I can publish them manually on Instagram.

User story US-09: As the content operator, I want a history of generated content with traceability from each exported slide back to its source data, so that I can revisit past content and show where every fact came from.

User story US-10: As the content operator, I want to manage reusable brand assets and carousel templates, and to have brand assets used only when they have actually been provided, so that the brand is applied consistently without placeholder or invented assets.

User story US-11: As the content operator, I want to supply match results, standings and competition, season and matchday data as JSON or CSV files or through a form in the web interface, so that I can cover competitions that have no public API (initial example: Liga Nacional de Guatemala).

User story US-12: As the content operator, I want the platform to retrieve competition data from football-data.org and to show for every fact whether it is VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED (for example awaiting independent verification) or MANUALLY_APPROVED, so that I know which facts are confirmed and which content can be approved.

User story US-13: As the content operator, I want a demonstration mode that runs the whole workflow on deterministic synthetic data, so that the platform can be developed, tested and demonstrated without a provider account or real data.

User story US-14: As the content operator, I want to pick any competition from one catalogue built from the configured providers and manual sources, then its season, its matchday or stage and one of its available data sources, so that I can cover different competitions and tournament formats with the same workflow.
The platform provides a web interface for managing content projects: the user can create a project, list the existing projects and open a project.
When creating a content project, the user selects a competition, a season and a matchday. In the MVP the only selectable competition is the UEFA Champions League (seasons and phases: R-417).

records.statement: For the selected competition, season and matchday, the Research Agent retrieves: the match results; the teams and scores of each match; the match dates; the competition standings; and relevant competition context.

relationships.target: ext:sports-data providers: a licensed sports-data API as preferred primary source and an independent official source for verification (PD-01, R-046), selected by the Architect (R-400) and authorized before any purchase or subscription (R-111)

records.statement: The user starts the research execution from the project and can follow its progress: the interface shows which workflow stage is pending, running, completed or failed, and a failed stage reports its reason.

Research results are stored as structured records. Each fact (for example a score, a match date or a standings row) carries its source attribution: the source it came from, a reference to its location in that source, and the retrieval time.

A Fact-Checking Agent independently verifies all factual information produced by research against reliable sources and records, for each fact, whether it is verified, the sources used and, when it is not verified, the reason. The verification rule is R-047 and R-048 (Product Owner decision PD-02) for scores, match dates and standings, and R-424 for other facts.

If a fact cannot be verified, publication approval is blocked for the content affected by that fact (every slide, headline, slide description or caption that uses it) until the fact is verified. Content that does not use the fact is not blocked. Changed in T11L (PD-17): the only exception is a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact of a competition configured as having no accepted public source, which does not block publication approval although it stays not verified (R-071); every other fact that is not verified, including a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact of a competition with an accepted API source, blocks as before.

The platform never invents scores, standings or match statistics. Every score, standing or match statistic that appears in generated content (slides, headlines, slide descriptions, captions) is taken from the verified data; content that contains such a value not present in the verified data is flagged and cannot be approved.
The platform clearly distinguishes verified facts from AI-generated commentary: each content element is identified as verified fact or generated commentary (presentation decided under R-404).
A Content Agent prepares, from the verified data: the carousel structure, the headlines, the slide descriptions, the social media captions and relevant hashtags.

relationships.target: ext:AI provider, to be selected by the Architect (R-401)

records.statement: A Graphic Design Agent creates the carousel slides: a cover slide, individual match-result slides (one per match), standings slides and a closing slide.
Slides are produced from reusable branded carousel templates; the same templates are reused across projects and matchdays.

Templates apply the El Deporte Rey GT identity: brand name El Deporte Rey GT, social handle @ElDeporteReyGT, mascot KETSI (images only when provided, R-034), and the colours purple, gold, blue and white.
The platform supports reusable brand assets: assets that have been provided (for example logos or mascot images) are registered once and reused by templates across projects.
Logos, team badges and mascot images are not assumed to exist; they are used only when they have been provided. Templates produce complete slides when such assets are absent.
Generated visuals preserve the exact verified scores and names: every score and name shown on a slide equals the verified value exactly (team names: the verified official names, R-052).

Numeric information is rendered deterministically: the same verified data and the same template always produce the same numeric text on the slide; numbers are never produced by a non-deterministic generation step.

A Visual QA Agent verifies every generated slide: scores and standings match the verified data; team names are correct; text fits the layout; visuals are consistent across the carousel; and the slide has the configured social media dimensions. Results are reported per slide and per check; failure handling is decided under R-420.
Before approving, the user can preview the generated carousel (all slides in carousel order) together with the captions and hashtags.
Explicit user approval is required before any content can be exported for publication; only approved assets can be exported (approval granularity: R-405; approval after a change: R-406).
The user can regenerate an individual slide without regenerating the other slides of the carousel.
The user can export approved assets for manual publication: the slide images and the captions with their hashtags.
The MVP does not publish automatically to any social platform; publication is done manually by the user from the exported files.
The platform keeps a history of generated content: past projects, with their generated slides, captions, approval state and exports, can be listed and reopened.
The platform maintains traceability from source data to exported slides: for every exported slide, the facts it shows, their verification status and their sources can be retrieved.

Facts are taken only from trustworthy, attributable data sources. The accepted sources are those set by Product Owner decision PD-01 (R-046): a licensed sports-data API as preferred primary source and an independent official source for verification.

Accepted data sources: research uses a licensed sports-data API as the preferred primary source, and fact-checking uses an independent official source for verification. Only accepted sources can make a fact verified (R-045). The providers that fill these roles are selected under R-400 and are not purchased or subscribed to without authorization (R-111). Changed in T11F: football-data.org API v4 fills the primary-source role (PD-12, R-053); the independent verification source is still to be approved (R-055, R-432); operator-supplied manual data is not an accepted source (R-071).
A score, a match date or a standings value is verified only when two independent accepted sources (R-046) agree on it. A value reported by only one accepted source is not verified.

When accepted sources disagree on a fact, the fact is marked disputed and is not verified; the official competition publication is consulted (R-311); the fact is not marked verified until the discrepancy is resolved (R-423). Content that uses a disputed fact stays blocked (R-026), and the user cannot mark the fact verified manually (R-412). Noted in T63 (PD-23, Product Owner 2026-10-28, risk U-08; this rule is unchanged): the provider research found no permitted automated access to a real official competition publication, so for WI-1 the consultation of a real official publication is not automated and no official page is scraped; for a real competition the consultation therefore finds no publication, and the fact stays UNVERIFIED (disputed) until a later retrieval shows two independent accepted sources in agreement (R-423); data the operator enters (MANUAL_DATA) never counts as an accepted source (R-071). The consultation of an official-publication source supplied as fixture data (R-205, R-230) is unchanged.

records.statement: Team names and the competition name appear in content as text. Slides use only existing brand assets that are authorized (R-309); no unauthorized logo, club badge or competition mark is used.

Templates reserve optional badge slots (for example one per team on a match-result slide). A badge slot shows an image only when an authorized badge asset exists for that team; until the Product Owner allows badges (R-413 option (b)) no badge is authorized, so the slots stay empty and the slides remain complete (R-034).

Each content project has a content language, which sets the language of the generated headlines, slide descriptions, captions and hashtags. The language is configurable per project; a new project uses Spanish unless the user selects another language (selectable languages: R-425).

Team names are preserved as verified official names: in every content language, every slide, headline, slide description and caption shows a team's name exactly as its verified official name, without translation, abbreviation or other change (source of the official name, hashtags and enforcement: R-426).

football-data.org API v4 (base URL https://api.football-data.org/v4) is the preferred primary sports-data provider of the MVP and its first concrete sports-data adapter (FootballDataProvider, the LIVE_DATA mode of R-056). The initial reference competition is the UEFA Champions League (provider code CL, provider ID 2001); these identifiers and the base URL are adapter configuration, not domain constants (R-139). It fills the primary-source role of R-046, not the independent verification role (R-055). It is introduced only after the security review and isolation decision of R-116.

Through FootballDataProvider the platform supports, for every competition the provider offers (R-073): competition discovery, available seasons, matchday or stage selection, match results, match status, team names, standings, source metadata and data retrieval timestamps (R-024). The adapter uses the provider capabilities for competition information, competition matches, matchday filtering, season filtering and competition standings; endpoint choice: R-437. Support for a data field or season is offered only after it is confirmed against the actual API (R-136).

The two-source verification policy (R-047, R-048) is preserved with football-data.org as the primary source: the Fact-Checking Agent verifies against an independent accepted source (R-046). Until a secondary source is approved and available (R-432), research may use football-data.org alone; its results are UNVERIFIED with the reason 'awaiting independent verification' (R-070), are never marked fully verified, and no publication approval is given on the basis of that single source (R-026). Changed in T11L (PD-18): also when an approved secondary source agrees and the facts are VERIFIED, content that uses football-data.org data is not publication-approvable until the republishing-permission confirmation of R-078 is recorded.

The platform supports three data acquisition modes: LIVE_DATA (data retrieved from external providers; initial provider football-data.org, R-053), MANUAL_DATA (data supplied by the operator, R-057) and DEMO_DATA (deterministic synthetic fixtures, R-058). Every content project uses one data source of its competition (selection: R-431, R-076); the mode and source are recorded on the project and in the source metadata of every fact (R-024).

In MANUAL_DATA mode the operator supplies sports data as JSON files, as CSV files, or as structured data entered through the web interface (R-020). The platform supports competitions without a public API through this mode; the initial example is Liga Nacional de Guatemala (format: R-434). Manual competitions appear in the same catalogue as API-backed ones (R-073). Imports follow R-060 to R-069 and R-119. It is introduced only after the security review and isolation decision of R-116.

In DEMO_DATA mode the platform uses deterministic synthetic fixtures for development, testing and demonstrations (FixtureDataProvider). DEMO_DATA is the default mode of the development configuration and of the default automated test suite (R-110, R-134); demonstration content is labelled as such (R-438).

All three modes and their adapters produce the same normalized, runtime-validated domain representation, built on the provider-neutral concepts of R-140 (R-105). The downstream stages (fact-checking, content, graphic design, visual QA, approval and export) do not depend on the selected mode, provider or competition; mode and provider appear only in source metadata.
Manual import rule 1: imported data (JSON files, CSV files and web-form entries) is validated at run time against schemas before it is stored or used (R-105).

Manual import rule 2: a failed validation gives clear errors; each error identifies the file or form, the record (for example the row or entry), the field and the problem, so that the operator can correct the data.
Manual import rule 3: malformed or incomplete records are rejected and are not stored or used (application of an import as a whole: R-435).
Manual import rule 4: duplicate match records are prevented; the same match (identity: R-435) is never stored twice for a competition, season and matchday or stage.
Manual import rule 5: imports carry competition, season and matchday (or stage, R-434) metadata, which the project selection (R-072) uses.
Manual import rule 6: imports carry match results (teams, status, the score of a finished match, date) and team-level standings.

Manual import rule 7: the original imported data (the file as received, or the submitted form entry) is preserved unchanged and linked to the data derived from it. Imports rejected under R-062 or R-119 are not stored.

Manual import rule 8: each import records its import timestamp and source metadata (the channel: JSON, CSV or web form; the file name where there is one; the source the operator declares the data was taken from); each fact from an import carries this attribution (R-024).

Manual import rule 9: the operator can correct data and import it again. A reimport creates a new version; earlier versions and their originals stay retrievable (R-066); approvals and MANUALLY_APPROVED statuses of changed facts do not carry over (R-406, R-435).

Manual import rule 10: missing scores or standings are never invented; the platform does not fill a missing score, derive standings that were not supplied or substitute a default value; a match without a score has no result, and a matchday or stage without standings has no standings content (R-027). This applies to every mode.

Every fact has one of three statuses: VERIFIED (two independent accepted sources agree, R-047), UNVERIFIED (not verified, with a reason such as 'awaiting independent verification' or 'disputed', R-048) or MANUALLY_APPROVED (operator approval of a MANUAL_DATA fact, R-071). Mapping to the existing verification states: R-433.

Manual approval is never represented as independent factual verification: a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact is never shown, stored, exported or traced as VERIFIED, and operator-supplied data is not an accepted source under R-046, so it never counts toward the agreement of R-047. Manual approval is an explicit operator action on a MANUAL_DATA fact, recorded with its time and the import it applies to; LIVE_DATA and disputed facts cannot be approved manually (R-412, R-048). Source attribution and auditability are preserved (R-024, R-044). Changed in T11L (PD-17, R-429 option (c); this replaces the earlier 'open (R-429)' sentence): content using a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact may pass publication approval only when the fact belongs to a competition configured as having no accepted public source (for example Liga Nacional de Guatemala, R-317); such a fact is always labelled operator-attested (R-320) and is never shown or stored as verified. A competition that has an accepted API source keeps the two-source rule (R-047, R-026), also when it has a MANUAL_DATA source as well (R-076): content using a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact of it cannot be approved. Whether a competition has no accepted public source is held in the competition configuration (where and how: for the Architect); a competition for which an accepted LIVE_DATA source is configured never counts as having none.

Replaces R-021 (confirmed by PD-19). When creating a content project, the operator selects a competition from the catalogue (R-073), a season, a matchday or equivalent stage (R-074) and one of the competition's available data sources (R-076, R-431). The catalogue holds the competitions of the configured LIVE_DATA providers (the UEFA Champions League is the initial reference scenario), the MANUAL_DATA competitions (initial example Liga Nacional de Guatemala) and, in DEMO_DATA configurations, the fixture competitions; no competition is hardcoded (R-139). The seasons and matchdays or stages offered are those the chosen source has data for.

Dynamic competition catalogue: the platform retrieves the available competitions from every configured LIVE_DATA provider and shows them, together with the MANUAL_DATA competitions and (in DEMO_DATA configurations) the fixture competitions, in one selectable catalogue; each entry shows its available data sources. Named competitions (UEFA Champions League, Spanish La Liga, English Premier League, German Bundesliga, Italian Serie A, French Ligue 1) are examples, not a fixed allow-list.

Seasons and matchdays or stages: for a selected competition the platform retrieves the available seasons; for a season, its matchdays or equivalent stages (for example league rounds, a group stage or knockout rounds, as the source names them); for a matchday or stage, its matches, results and, where the competition provides them, standings. Competitions with different tournament structures are handled through the same flow (scope reading: R-439).

Unavailable competitions, unsupported features and subscription restrictions are detected and shown with a reason: a competition or season the configured subscription does not grant, or a feature a competition or source does not offer (for example standings for a stage), is marked unavailable or unsupported in the catalogue and selection views; no data is invented for it (R-069) and other competitions are unaffected.

A competition may have one or more configured data sources; the operator chooses an available one for a project (R-431). The source used is recorded for traceability on the project, on every retrieval (provider request or import) and on every fact (R-024, R-044).

The interface and the content workflow do not assume one competition format: a matchday or stage without standings shows its matches and results and states that standings are not available, and its carousel has no standings slide (R-030) and is otherwise complete; stage and matchday names are shown as the source provides them; every workflow (selection, research, verification, content, preview, approval, export) is reusable across competitions.

Republishing permission for football-data.org content (PD-18, R-430 option (a)): before content that uses football-data.org data is approved for publication, the Product Owner obtains written confirmation of republishing permission from the provider, including any attribution requirement, and records it as a Product Owner decision. Until that decision is recorded, LIVE_DATA content from that provider is not publication-approvable: approval of a slide, headline, slide description, caption or carousel that uses a football-data.org fact is refused with the reason 'republishing permission not confirmed'; content that uses no such fact is not affected. An attribution requirement brought by the confirmation becomes a template requirement through a later requirements change. How the recorded decision is made known to the platform is for the Architect. No legal assessment is given here.

records.statement: The MVP is local-first: the platform and its data run on the user's local machine (access to external providers: R-306).
MVP scope priorities, in order: (1) one competition, the UEFA Champions League; (2) matchday results and standings; (3) Instagram carousel generation; (4) manual approval and export.

records.statement: The technology stack is not prescribed by the Product Owner; the Architect proposes it based on these requirements.
Modular architecture with testable agent boundaries: each workflow stage (research, fact-checking, content, graphic design, visual QA) has defined inputs and outputs and can be tested in isolation.
Strong runtime validation: data received from providers and data exchanged between workflow stages is validated at run time against its expected structure; invalid data is rejected and not used.
Provider abstraction: AI providers and sports-data providers are configurable and can be replaced through configuration without changing the workflow stages.
Automated testing: the platform has automated tests covering the workflow stages and the business rules of this document.
Local development: the platform can be developed, run and tested on a local machine.
Avoid unnecessary infrastructure and premature complexity: the MVP introduces no component that the MVP scope (R-101) does not need.

During development, research and verification run on synthetic fixture data supplied through the provider abstraction (R-106), not on data from real sports-data providers; the default automated test suite uses synthetic fixtures only (R-225). Changed in T11F: this is the DEMO_DATA mode (R-058), the default of the development configuration; optional live integration tests (R-135), run only when explicitly enabled, are outside the default suite.

No service (a sports-data API, an AI provider or any other service) is purchased or subscribed to without authorization from the Product Owner. Changed in T11F: this includes purchasing or upgrading a football-data.org subscription (PD-12). Noted in T63 (PD-22, Product Owner 2026-10-28, answer to E-15 DR-2; this constraint is unchanged): no cost is authorized; the football-data.org free plan stays, and no account, trial, subscription or upgrade is made for any service, including the secondary-source candidates of R-432 and a hosted AI provider (R-401).

records.statement: The MVP is limited to team-level and competition-level data. No player-level information (for example player names, goal scorers, line-ups or player statistics) is collected, stored, generated or shown, and no personal data of users is kept (R-113).

The MVP has a single local operator and no login: the platform has no user accounts, no sign-in step and no user management. Changed in T11L: confirmed for LIVE_DATA with the real provider token by PD-16, under the conditions and re-raise triggers of R-143.

Development services are bound to localhost only: the web interface and every other network service the platform starts listen only on the loopback interface and accept no connection from another machine (the web interface in MVP use as well, R-415 option (a)).

Processing of untrusted input inside the platform process (Product Owner decision PD-10). Within WI-1's scope (sports data from synthetic fixtures (R-110), the stub or a local AI provider, and operator-supplied PNG or JPEG brand files (R-033)), provider data, AI output and brand files may be parsed and decoded inside the platform process without thread or process isolation, provided these compensating controls are in place: allow-list schemas for provider data and AI output (R-105); size, dimension and timeout caps; file-signature checks on brand files; SVG files refused; no HTML parsing; inputs to slide rendering supplied as data URIs only; and an egress lint rule that confines network access. The acceptance is limited to this scope (R-116).

Condition of Product Owner decision PD-10: before the first real sports-data adapter, any hosted AI provider, or any new input type (for example SVG, HTML or web scraping, or archives) is introduced, a new security review is carried out and the Product Owner takes a new decision on the isolation of untrusted-input processing. Until then, R-115 does not cover them. Changed in T11F: PD-12 and PD-13 (S-003) bring a real sports-data adapter (FootballDataProvider, R-053) and new input types (operator-supplied JSON and CSV files and web-form data entry, R-057) into WI-1's scope, so the condition applies within WI-1: they are not introduced before the new security review and the Product Owner's decision on isolation. The T11B reading (WI-1 delivers no real adapter and no new input type, security design review control V-30) no longer holds; how V-30 is restated is for that security review. Changed in T11L: the new security review has been carried out (T11H) and the Product Owner has decided on isolation for FootballDataProvider responses and for the JSON, CSV and web-form imports (PD-15, option A: in-process processing under the conditions of R-142), so the condition is met for these inputs. It still applies to any hosted AI provider and any other new input type, and R-142 adds further triggers for a new review and decision.

Contract-evolution policy of the http-api contract (Product Owner decision PD-11). Within version v1 only additive changes are made: new optional request fields, new response fields, new operations and new problem codes. Removing an operation, a field or a problem code, or changing its meaning, is a breaking change; a breaking change needs a new major version path and a Product Owner decision. A new required request field or header is not an additive change.

Provider-independent ingestion interface: the existing provider abstraction (R-106) is preserved; sports data enters through one ingestion interface with the adapters FootballDataProvider (LIVE_DATA), ManualDataProvider (MANUAL_DATA) and FixtureDataProvider (DEMO_DATA), which all produce the validated domain representation of R-059. A further provider is added as a new adapter without changing the Research Agent's business logic.

Privacy (PD-04 applied to PD-12 and PD-13): only team-level and competition-level data enters the platform in any mode. Provider responses are mapped through an allow-list of team- and competition-level fields; person data a provider may return (for example referees, coaches, squads or goal scorers) is dropped at the adapter and is not stored, cached, logged or passed on; the request cache holds mapped projections only (R-132). A manual import that contains a person-level field is rejected with a validation error naming the field (R-061), so a preserved original (R-066) never holds person data. No personal data is processed (R-414).

Security (PD-12): FootballDataProvider authenticates with a token read from the environment variable FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN and sent in the X-Auth-Token request header; provider requests are made from the platform's server side only. The token is handled under R-121 to R-127.
Credential rule 1: API credentials are never hardcoded; no credential value appears in source code, committed configuration, fixtures or tests.
Credential rule 2: credentials are never committed to Git.
Credential rule 3: credentials are never exposed to the frontend; no token is in the browser assets, in http-api responses or in requests made by the browser.
Credential rule 4: credentials never appear in logs or test evidence, including error messages, problem responses, diagnostic logs, test reports and task evidence.
Credential rule 5: the repository provides an .env.example file that names FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN without a real credential.
Credential rule 6: local credential files (for example .env) are Git-ignored.
Credential rule 7: the configuration is validated at application startup (outcome when the token is missing: R-436); validation messages name a missing or invalid variable, never its value.

Every provider response is validated at run time against its expected structure before it is mapped to the domain representation (R-059) through the allow-list of R-119; a response that fails validation is rejected and not used (R-105).

HTTP error handling and timeouts: every provider request has a timeout; provider errors (bad request, restricted resource, not found, too many requests, server error) and timeouts end the request with a classified reason that the research stage reports (R-023) without credential data.

Bounded retries: transient failures (timeouts, network errors, server errors, and too-many-requests responses after the counter reset) are retried a bounded number of times; authentication, access and not-found errors are not retried; retries never exceed the rate limit (R-131). Counts and back-off: R-437.

Rate-limit handling: the adapter reads the rate-limit headers X-RequestsAvailable and X-RequestCounter-Reset on every response, makes no request while the available count is exhausted before the counter reset, handles a too-many-requests response by waiting for the reset, and keeps within a configured request budget (R-312); unlimited API access is never assumed.

Request caching: provider results are cached for a configured validity period (R-437) so that repeated requests for the same resource do not reach the provider; the cache holds only mapped team- and competition-level projections with their retrieval time (R-119), no credential, and no error or invalid response.
Safe diagnostic logging: provider calls are logged with enough detail to diagnose failures (resource, status, timing, rate-limit header values) and without credentials or person data (R-124, R-119).

Testing: deterministic fixtures are the default test mode (DEMO_DATA, R-058); contract tests check FootballDataProvider against recorded football-data.org responses for valid responses, missing optional fields, invalid responses, authentication failures, rate-limit responses, provider unavailability, network timeouts, cache behaviour, unavailable competitions or seasons, missing standings, incomplete matchdays and provider data disagreements.

Live API integration tests are optional: they run only when explicitly enabled and a token is configured, are not part of the default test suite or of any gate, stay within the rate limit, and expose no credential in output, reports or evidence (R-124). A credential-safe capability probe of the same kind confirms the provider capabilities of R-136.

Provider capabilities and conditions are verified, not assumed: support for a data field, season or competition is promised only after it is confirmed against the actual API with the Product Owner's subscription (capability probe, R-135). Findings on competition availability (the Champions League and the other competitions offered), match and standings coverage, available seasons, rate limits, data freshness, commercial-use conditions, republishing restrictions and attribution requirements are recorded with their sources; an item that cannot be confirmed is recorded as unverified (R-312 to R-316). API access is not taken as permission to redistribute the supplied content (R-430; decided by PD-18: publication waits for the written confirmation of R-078). No subscription is purchased or upgraded (R-111).

Replaces R-101 (confirmed by PD-19). Security (PD-15, isolation of untrusted-input processing, option A for both inputs): FootballDataProvider responses and the MANUAL_DATA imports (JSON files, CSV files and web-form entries) are processed inside the platform process, without thread or process isolation, under these conditions: (1) the size caps, processing deadline, processing order and schemas set for these inputs by the T11H security review are in place; (2) an adversarial test corpus for the CSV parser and the JSON pre-scan, and a timing test showing roughly linear processing time up to the size cap, are part of the tests; if the timing test cannot be met, worker-thread isolation (option B) becomes the fallback for the imports through a re-plan; (3) no new parser dependency (for example a CSV, XML, spreadsheet or archive library) and no native decoder is added; (4) a new security review and a new Product Owner isolation decision are needed before a new input format (for example XLSX, ODS, XML, HTML or scraping, PDF or archives), before any size cap is raised above 2 MiB or any import limit is raised, before a second real provider adapter (including the independent verification source of R-432), before a hosted AI provider, and before the platform runs on a shared or multi-user host.

Security, identity model (PD-16, option A): the no-login model of R-113 is confirmed for LIVE_DATA with the real FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN under these conditions: the platform runs on a single-user workstation; the token is a free-plan token only (no paid plan, R-111); the local credential file .env.local is readable and writable by its owner only (mode 0600); the LIVE_DATA configuration is enabled only when needed; and the request-budget controls of the T11H security review are in place (rate-limit header values bounded, out-of-bound values ignored; discovery limited to part of the per-minute budget, with research and verification taking priority; one provider request at a time per cache key; a bound on queued discovery requests; unknown competition or season identifiers answered without a provider request). The competition selector is the catalogue of R-073: it offers the competitions of every configured LIVE_DATA provider, every MANUAL_DATA competition (in the default configuration Liga Nacional de Guatemala) and, in DEMO_DATA configurations, the fixture competitions, each with its available data sources; the season selector offers only seasons the chosen source has; the matchday-or-stage selector lists only matchdays or stages of the selected season; a project cannot be created until competition, season, matchday or stage, and data source are all selected.

Contract test, valid responses: recorded valid football-data.org responses for competition information, matches filtered by season and matchday, and standings are mapped to the domain representation with every match's teams, status, score of finished matches and date, and every standings row, equal to the recorded values; each fact carries source metadata (provider, resource, competition) and its retrieval timestamp.

Contract test, missing optional fields: a recorded response from which optional fields are removed (for example a team's short name or the standings form) is accepted; the missing values stay absent in the domain representation and no default or invented value replaces them.

Contract test, invalid responses: a response that is not valid JSON, lacks a required field (for example a team of a match or the score of a finished match), has a wrong type or has an unknown match status is rejected with a validation error; the research stage fails with a reason and nothing from that response is stored or used.

Contract test, authentication failures: when the stub refuses the request as unauthenticated or restricted (HTTP 401 or 403 with an error body), the request is not retried, the research stage fails with a reason saying provider access was refused, and neither the reason nor the logs contain the token.

Contract test, rate limits: the adapter records X-RequestsAvailable and X-RequestCounter-Reset from every response; when X-RequestsAvailable reaches 0, or the stub answers 429 with X-RequestCounter-Reset set to N, no further request is sent until N seconds have passed (controllable clock), after which the adapter continues or fails with a rate-limit reason; in a test run the requests in any 60-second window never exceed the configured budget.

Contract test, provider unavailability: when the stub answers with server errors or refuses connections, the adapter retries at most the configured number of times, then the research stage fails with a reason naming provider unavailability, and the operator can start research again.

Contract test, network timeouts: when the stub delays its answer beyond the configured timeout, the request is aborted at the timeout and retried within the retry bound, and the stage then fails with a timeout reason; the total time is bounded by the timeout and retry settings.

Contract test, cache behaviour: a second identical request within the validity period is answered from the cache without a request to the stub and with the original retrieval timestamp; after the validity period a new request is made; error and invalid responses are not cached; the cache holds no token, no request header and no person-level field.

Contract test, unavailable competitions or seasons: for a competition or season the stub reports as restricted (403) or not found (404), or a season absent from the competition's season list, research reports that it is not available with the current subscription, makes no retry and produces no data.

Contract test, missing standings: when the standings resource returns no table for the season or matchday, research records the standings as unavailable with a reason; no standings value is invented or derived, no standings slide is generated from missing data, and content that does not use standings is not affected.

Contract test, incomplete matchdays: for a recorded matchday in which some matches are not finished (for example scheduled, in play, postponed, suspended or cancelled), every provider status value is mapped to a domain status, only finished matches have a result, and unfinished matches are listed with their status and get no match-result slide (R-409).

Contract test, provider data disagreements: given a football-data.org fixture and an independent verification-source fixture that disagree on a score, the fact is UNVERIFIED (disputed) and the dispute procedure of R-048 and R-230 applies; when they agree, the fact is VERIFIED and cites both sources.

The default automated test suite runs with DEMO_DATA and without FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN set, makes no network request to api.football-data.org (checked by the test harness), and gives the same results on repeated runs.

Live API integration tests are skipped unless explicitly enabled with the token set; no default suite or gate runs them; when run, their console output, test reports and evidence files contain no token value (checked by scanning for the configured value), and they make no more requests than the configured budget.

The optional capability probe, run with the Product Owner's token, records with its date and the resource queried: the competitions the token can access (including the reference competition, configured as CL, 2001), the available seasons, matchday filtering, standings availability, the presence of each field the mapping uses, and the observed rate-limit header values; its output contains no token value; a field, season or competition it does not confirm is treated as unsupported.

Credential rule 1: with FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN set to a synthetic marker value, every request to the stub carries the marker in the X-Auth-Token header and nowhere else (not in the URL or query); a scan of source code, committed configuration, fixtures and tests finds no credential value.
Credential rule 2: the project's secret scan over the committed tree reports no finding, and no file matching the local credential file patterns is tracked by Git.

Credential rule 3: with a synthetic marker token configured, the built frontend assets, every http-api response and the browser's network requests contain no occurrence of the marker, and the browser makes no request to api.football-data.org.

Credential rule 4: with a synthetic marker token configured, after success, authentication-failure, rate-limit, timeout and validation-failure scenarios, the application logs, error messages, problem responses, test reports and evidence files contain no occurrence of the marker; diagnostic log entries for provider calls show the X-Auth-Token header redacted or absent.
Credential rule 5: the repository contains .env.example, which names FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN with an empty or clearly placeholder value that is not a credential.
Credential rule 6: git check-ignore reports the local credential files (for example .env and .env.local) as ignored, while .env.example is tracked.

Credential rule 7: with LIVE_DATA enabled and FOOTBALL_DATA_API_TOKEN missing or empty, the application does not start and reports the variable by name without any value; an unknown data mode or another invalid setting also stops startup with a named error; with LIVE_DATA not enabled, the application starts without the token.

The same synthetic matchday (matches, results, statuses and standings) supplied through FixtureDataProvider, through ManualDataProvider as a JSON file, as a CSV file and as web-form entries, and through FootballDataProvider from recorded stub responses, gives domain representations that pass the same runtime schema and are equal apart from mode, source metadata and timestamps.

The fact-checking, content, graphic design and visual QA stages run unchanged on the representation of every mode; the architecture review confirms that all adapters implement the one ingestion interface and that the Research Agent's business logic has no provider-specific branch, so a new provider is added as an adapter only.

Each project shows its data acquisition mode, and every fact's source metadata names the mode and the provider or import it came from; a DEMO_DATA project and its exports are labelled as demonstration content (R-438).

With fixtures: a value on which two independent accepted sources agree is VERIFIED; a value from football-data.org alone is UNVERIFIED with the reason 'awaiting independent verification'; a MANUAL_DATA value is UNVERIFIED until the operator approves it and MANUALLY_APPROVED afterwards; every fact has exactly one of the three statuses.

With LIVE_DATA and no secondary source configured, research completes, its facts are UNVERIFIED with the reason 'awaiting independent verification' and never VERIFIED, and approval of any slide, headline, caption or carousel that uses them is refused with a reason naming the single-source fact. Changed in T11L (PD-18): with an independent secondary source configured and agreeing, so that the facts are VERIFIED, approval of content that uses a football-data.org fact is still refused with the reason 'republishing permission not confirmed' while no republishing-permission confirmation is recorded (R-078), and is no longer refused for that reason once it is recorded.

A MANUALLY_APPROVED fact is shown in the review view, stored, and reported in traceability and export metadata as MANUALLY_APPROVED, never as VERIFIED; it does not count toward two-source agreement; its audit record shows the approval time and the import and declared source it came from; manual approval of a LIVE_DATA fact or a disputed fact is refused. Changed in T11L (PD-17; this replaces the earlier 'until R-429 is decided' sentence): for a competition configured as having no accepted public source, content using a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact can be approved for publication and the fact is labelled operator-attested in the review view and in traceability and export metadata; for a competition with an accepted API source, also when it has a MANUAL_DATA source too, approval of content using a MANUALLY_APPROVED fact is refused with a reason naming the fact (R-026).

Manual import rules 1 and 3: a JSON file that does not parse, a CSV file with missing or unknown columns, and a record with a missing required field, a wrong type or an impossible value (for example a negative score) are each rejected by schema validation; nothing from a rejected import is stored or used (R-435).

Manual import rule 2: every validation error names the file or form, the record (CSV row number or JSON entry), the field and the problem with the expected form; all errors of an import are reported together.

Manual import rule 4: an import containing the same match twice is rejected with a duplicate-match error naming both records; importing a match that already exists for the same competition, season and matchday or stage adds no second match record (corrections go through reimport, R-278).

Manual import rules 5 and 6: a valid import with competition, season and matchday (or stage) metadata, match results and standings is accepted; that competition, season and matchday or stage can then be selected for a project and research returns the imported matches, results and standings; an import without competition, season or matchday-or-stage metadata is rejected.

Manual import rules 7 and 8: after an import the original file, or the submitted form entry, is retrievable unchanged (same content hash) and linked to the import record, which shows the import timestamp, the channel, the file name and the declared source; every fact from the import traces back to it.

Manual import rule 9: correcting a score and importing again creates a new import version used by later research; the earlier version and its original remain retrievable; the changed fact loses its MANUALLY_APPROVED status, and content using it needs QA and approval again (R-406).

Manual import rule 10: a finished match without a score is rejected as incomplete; a match that is not finished is stored without a score and gets no match-result slide; when no standings are imported, none are produced or derived; no stored or generated value fills a missing score or standing.

Given a recorded football-data.org response that includes person data (for example referees, coaches, squads or goal scorers), the domain representation, the cache, the stored data and the logs contain none of it; a manual import that contains a person-level field (for example a player or scorer column) is rejected with an error naming the field and nothing from it is stored.

The provider findings record (Architect deliverable, R-136) lists for football-data.org: competition availability (the Champions League and the other competitions offered), match and standings coverage, available seasons, rate limits, data freshness, commercial-use conditions, republishing restrictions and attribution requirements, each with its source and date or marked unverified; no subscription has been purchased or upgraded.

Catalogue: with a stub LIVE_DATA provider listing several competitions, an imported MANUAL_DATA competition and the DEMO_DATA fixtures, the catalogue shows all of them in one list, each with its available data sources; a competition that a stub response adds appears without any code change, and one it removes disappears.

Seasons and stages: for a stub league competition the selector lists its matchdays; for a stub competition organised in stages (for example a group stage and knockout rounds) it lists the stages under the names the source gives; selecting each returns its matches and results, with standings only where the source provides them.

Replaces R-239. For the reference competition (recorded responses), every matchday or stage the source reports for the selected season is selectable, including stages after the league phase; for a stage without standings the review view shows its matches and results and states that standings are not available, and no view shows an empty or invented standings table.

Replaces R-210. The generated carousel contains a cover slide, one match-result slide for each match included in the carousel structure, at least one standings slide when the selected matchday or stage has verified standings and none when it has no standings, and a closing slide; a carousel without standings passes Visual QA and can be approved and exported under the same rules as any other.

Unavailable competitions and features: when the stub answers 403 for a listed competition's resources, the catalogue marks that competition unavailable for the current subscription with a reason; when a competition or stage has no standings or no season history, the feature is shown as not available; no data is invented, and the other competitions remain usable.

Source recorded: for a competition configured with two data sources, the operator can choose either at project creation; the project, every retrieval (provider request or import) and every fact record the source used, and the traceability view of an exported slide shows it.

Provider-neutral contracts: the shared domain schema and the http-api contract define Competition, Season, Stage, Matchday, Match, Team, Standing, Source and Verification status with no football-data.org-specific field name or identifier; provider-specific data appears only in adapter-side types; the outputs of FootballDataProvider, ManualDataProvider and FixtureDataProvider all validate against the same shared schema.

No hardcoded competition: an automated static check scans every source file outside the provider adapters and the configuration (domain modules, core services, workflow stages, UI) and fails when it finds a competition identifier used as a constant, including the Champions League code CL, the ID 2001, the host api.football-data.org or the competition name used in logic; a seeded violation makes the check fail, and the check passes on the delivered code.

Multi-competition demonstration: the same workflow code takes at least two distinct LIVE_DATA competitions, one MANUAL_DATA competition and one DEMO_DATA competition through selection, retrieval, provenance and status review, content generation and preview, and approval and export as far as the verification rules allow (R-055, R-071); deterministic tests use recorded provider responses for both LIVE_DATA competitions, and the live run is subject to the coverage the capability probe confirms (R-440).

Discovery within the rate limit: with a budget of 10 requests per minute and a stub provider listing many competitions, showing the catalogue and selecting competitions never exceeds the budget in any 60-second window; showing the catalogue makes no per-competition request; a second view within the cache validity makes no request; when the budget is exhausted the cached lists are shown with their retrieval time or the wait until the counter reset is reported.

records.statement: When is a disputed fact (R-048) resolved, so that it can be marked verified?

relationships.target: ext:Product Owner decision PD-23 (tracker Decisions table; Product Owner 2026-10-28, answer to E-15 DR-4, risk U-08)

records.resolution: Applying PD-02 (S-001 lines 13-19) as a whole: a disputed fact is resolved when a single value is supported by two independent accepted sources, for example when the official competition publication (R-311) agrees with one of the disagreeing sources, or when a later retrieval shows the sources in agreement. The verification stage records the disagreeing values, the consultation and the outcome. If the official publication is unavailable, gives no value, gives a third value, or is the same source as one of the disagreeing ones, no value has two independent accepted sources, so the fact stays disputed and not verified and the affected content stays blocked (R-026). The user can re-run verification but cannot set the value or mark the fact verified manually (R-412). Applied for WI-1 by PD-23 (Product Owner 2026-10-28, answer to E-15 DR-4, risk U-08): the consultation of a real official competition publication is not automated and no official page is scraped, so for real competitions the 'official publication unavailable' case applies: a disagreement between two accepted sources stays UNVERIFIED (disputed) until a later retrieval shows agreement; data the operator enters (MANUAL_DATA) never counts as an accepted source (R-071).
records.basis: S-001 lines 14-15 (agreement of two independent accepted sources is required) and 17-19 (consult the official competition publication; disputed facts are not verified until the discrepancy is resolved); S-000 lines 89-90; R-412. PD-23 is recorded in the tracker Decisions table (Product Owner 2026-10-28, answer to E-15 DR-4; no intake source file); context: docs/work-items/WI-1/architecture/provider-research.md sections 3.4, 6.2 and 9 DR-4 (T14, not an intake source).

workItems.title: Phase 1: Foundation - local web interface for a single operator without login and bound to localhost, content projects with a dynamic competition catalogue and selection of season, matchday or stage and data source, provider-neutral domain model and ingestion interface with DEMO_DATA fixtures and stub providers, credential handling and startup validation, runtime validation, automated test harness (Initial Scope priority 1)

Phase 2: Verified matchday or stage results and standings - research through FootballDataProvider (LIVE_DATA) and ManualDataProvider (MANUAL_DATA), source attribution, two-source fact-checking with the dispute procedure and the VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED and MANUALLY_APPROVED statuses, team- and competition-level data only (Initial Scope priority 2)

Phase 3: Instagram carousel generation - content drafting in the project language, branded templates with badge slots and authorized assets, carousels with or without standings, deterministic slide rendering at 1080 x 1350, visual QA (Initial Scope priority 3)
Phase 4: Review, per-slide and caption approval with final approval, manual export, history and traceability, and the multi-competition demonstration (Initial Scope priority 4)
